```{r}
#| label: setup
acceptance_dir <- file.path(
  "..", "outputs", "goal002", "frozen", "acceptance"
)
required_evidence <- file.path(
  acceptance_dir,
  c(
    "criteria.csv",
    "gate-object.rds",
    "validated-results.rds",
    "validation-provenance.rds",
    "provenance.csv",
    "validation-checks.csv",
    "status-counts.csv"
  )
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(required_evidence)))

gate <- readRDS(file.path(acceptance_dir, "gate-object.rds"))
results <- readRDS(file.path(acceptance_dir, "validated-results.rds"))
validation <- readRDS(
  file.path(acceptance_dir, "validation-provenance.rds")
)
criteria_frozen <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(acceptance_dir, "criteria.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)
provenance <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(acceptance_dir, "provenance.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
status_counts <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(acceptance_dir, "status-counts.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
prior_assessment <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(
    "..", "outputs", "goal002", "prior-predictive",
    "automatic-assessment.csv"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
prior_manifest <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(
    "..", "outputs", "goal002", "prior-predictive",
    "run-manifest.csv"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(results) == 96L,
  sum(results$run_type == "primary") == 60L,
  sum(results$run_type == "sensitivity") == 36L,
  !anyDuplicated(results$run_id),
  all(results$artifacts_verified),
  identical(criteria_frozen$criterion, 19:35),
  sum(criteria_frozen$passed) == 14L,
  identical(criteria_frozen$criterion[!criteria_frozen$passed], c(27L, 33L, 34L)),
  nrow(prior_assessment) == 21L,
  all(prior_assessment$passed)
)

profile_id <- c(
  primary = "primary-v1",
  sensitivity_membership = "sensitivity-membership-v1",
  sensitivity_tail = "sensitivity-tail-v2"
)
duration_label <- c(`26` = "six months", `208` = "four years")

format_count <- function(numerator, denominator) {
  paste0(numerator, "/", denominator)
}

format_range <- function(x, digits = 2L) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0L) {
    return("suppressed")
  }
  value <- range(x)
  paste0(
    formatC(value[1L], format = "f", digits = digits),
    "–",
    formatC(value[2L], format = "f", digits = digits)
  )
}

summary_objects <- lapply(
  results$summary_path,
  function(path) readRDS(file.path("..", path))
)

diagnostic_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(results)),
  function(index) {
    diagnostics <- summary_objects[[index]]$diagnostics$terminal_attempt
    metrics <- diagnostics$metrics
    tibble::tibble(
      run_id = results$run_id[index],
      run_type = results$run_type[index],
      prior_profile = results$prior_profile[index],
      true_richness = results$true_richness[index],
      n_occasions = results$n_occasions[index],
      replicate = results$replicate[index],
      terminal_status = results$terminal_status[index],
      rescue_used = results$rescue_used[index],
      clean = diagnostics$clean,
      reasons = if (length(diagnostics$reasons)) {
        paste(diagnostics$reasons, collapse = ", ")
      } else {
        "none"
      },
      divergences = metrics$divergences,
      treedepth_hits = metrics$treedepth_hits,
      min_ebfmi = metrics$min_ebfmi,
      max_rhat = metrics$max_rhat,
      min_bulk_ess = metrics$min_bulk_ess,
      min_tail_ess = metrics$min_tail_ess
    )
  }
))

ppc_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(results)),
  function(index) {
    summary <- summary_objects[[index]]
    if (identical(summary$terminal_status, "final_nonclean")) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    total <- summary$posterior_predictive$total_detections
    tibble::tibble(
      run_id = results$run_id[index],
      run_type = results$run_type[index],
      prior_profile = results$prior_profile[index],
      true_richness = results$true_richness[index],
      n_occasions = results$n_occasions[index],
      observed_richness = results$observed_richness[index],
      posterior_mean_richness = summary$richness$mean,
      observed_total_detections = total$observed,
      replicated_mean_detections = total$replicated_mean,
      replicated_q05 = total$replicated_q05,
      replicated_q95 = total$replicated_q95,
      observed_in_replication_90 = total$observed >= total$replicated_q05 &
        total$observed <= total$replicated_q95
    )
  }
))

primary <- gate$primary_gate_values |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    clean = terminal_status != "final_nonclean",
    profile_id = profile_id[prior_profile],
    duration = unname(duration_label[as.character(n_occasions)])
  )

primary_cell <- primary |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    run_type, profile_id, cell_id, true_richness, n_occasions, duration
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    planned_n = dplyr::n(),
    clean_n = sum(.data$clean),
    nonclean_n = sum(!.data$clean),
    rescues_n = sum(.data$rescue_used),
    observed_median = stats::median(.data$observed_richness),
    observed_range = format_range(.data$observed_richness, 0L),
    posterior_mean_median = stats::median(
      .data$posterior_mean[.data$clean],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    posterior_mean_range = format_range(
      .data$posterior_mean[.data$clean],
      2L
    ),
    coverage_90 = sum(.data$covered_90),
    median_absolute_error = stats::median(.data$absolute_error),
    raw_median_absolute_error = stats::median(
      abs(.data$observed_richness - .data$true_richness)
    ),
    median_interval_width = stats::median(
      .data$interval_width[.data$clean],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    median_rps = stats::median(.data$rps),
    median_baseline_rps = stats::median(.data$baseline_rps),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Independently reconstruct every displayed primary-cell statistic using base
# indexing. This guards against dplyr's sequential summarise name masking.
primary_cell_direct <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
  split(primary, primary$cell_id),
  function(cell) {
    keep <- cell$terminal_status != "final_nonclean"
    tibble::tibble(
      run_type = unique(cell$run_type),
      profile_id = unique(cell$profile_id),
      cell_id = unique(cell$cell_id),
      true_richness = unique(cell$true_richness),
      n_occasions = unique(cell$n_occasions),
      duration = unique(cell$duration),
      planned_n = nrow(cell),
      clean_n = sum(keep),
      nonclean_n = sum(!keep),
      rescues_n = sum(cell$rescue_used),
      observed_median = stats::median(cell$observed_richness),
      observed_range = format_range(cell$observed_richness, 0L),
      posterior_mean_median = stats::median(
        cell$posterior_mean[keep],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      posterior_mean_range = format_range(
        cell$posterior_mean[keep],
        2L
      ),
      coverage_90 = sum(cell$covered_90),
      median_absolute_error = stats::median(cell$absolute_error),
      raw_median_absolute_error = stats::median(
        abs(cell$observed_richness - cell$true_richness)
      ),
      median_interval_width = stats::median(
        cell$interval_width[keep],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      median_rps = stats::median(cell$rps),
      median_baseline_rps = stats::median(cell$baseline_rps)
    )
  }
))

primary_cell_check <- primary_cell |>
  dplyr::arrange(cell_id) |>
  as.data.frame()
primary_cell_direct_check <- primary_cell_direct |>
  dplyr::arrange(cell_id) |>
  as.data.frame()
row.names(primary_cell_check) <- NULL
row.names(primary_cell_direct_check) <- NULL

cell_1_check <- primary_cell_direct |>
  dplyr::filter(cell_id == 1L)
cell_4_source <- primary |>
  dplyr::filter(cell_id == 4L)
cell_4_keep <- cell_4_source$terminal_status != "final_nonclean"

stopifnot(
  identical(primary_cell_check, primary_cell_direct_check),
  nrow(primary_cell_direct) == 6L,
  identical(cell_1_check$clean_n, 9L),
  identical(cell_1_check$nonclean_n, 1L),
  abs(
    stats::median(cell_4_source$posterior_mean[cell_4_keep]) -

  abs(min(cell_4_source$posterior_mean[cell_4_keep]) - 7.333324) < 1e-6,
  abs(max(cell_4_source$posterior_mean[cell_4_keep]) - 10.634249) < 1e-6,

    stats::median(cell_4_source$interval_width[cell_4_keep]),

)

criteria_closure <- tibble::tribble(

criteria_table <- criteria_frozen |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    criterion,
    numerator,
    denominator,
    statistic = as.character(signif(statistic, 10L)),
    threshold,
    verdict = ifelse(passed, "PASS", "FAIL"),
    evidence_id = paste0("FROZEN:criteria.csv#C", criterion)

  dplyr::bind_rows(criteria_closure) |>
  dplyr::arrange(criterion) |>

  dplyr::select(
    criterion, fraction, statistic, threshold, verdict, evidence_id
  )
```

The frozen 96-fit experiment completed, but the prespecified scientific gate
failed Criteria 27, 33 and 34. Goal 002 therefore closes as an **informative
method failure**, not as a blocked computation and not as approval to tune or
rerun the pilot.

## Estimand, model and interpretation boundary

The estimand is whole-grid detectable-use richness,
\(S_{\mathrm{grid}}=\sum_i g_i\), for a finite known pool of 30 eligible
candidate species. Observed richness, \(S_{\mathrm{obs}}\), counts candidates
detected at least once and is a hard lower bound. Known true richness is
available only because these are correctly specified simulations; it never
enters the fitted data.

The fitted model analytically marginalises candidate membership, uses
effort-aware binary detection with exact active camera-days, and estimates
species and sum-to-zero camera effects on the log encounter-rate scale. The
primary richness distribution is the Rao--Blackwellised Poisson-binomial mass
function averaged over continuous posterior draws. `final_nonclean` rows
retain diagnostics but expose no posterior inference.

This report supports only implementation correctness and the recorded
best-case behaviour under the Goal 001 synthetic family. It does not
demonstrate empirical validity, robustness to misspecification,
candidate-pool completeness, correct unseen-species identities, universal
calibration, or superiority to another estimator.

## Frozen design and status accounting

The frozen design contains 60 primary fits (10 replicates in each of six
duration-by-truth cells) and 36 prespecified sensitivities (three paired
replicates per cell for each of two profiles). All 96 terminal records and
1,129 retained artifact paths passed the independent acceptance validation.

```{r}
#| label: table-status-counts
status_table <- status_counts |>
  dplyr::mutate(profile_id = profile_id[prior_profile]) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Terminal status` = terminal_status,
    `Rows` = n
  )
knitr::kable(
  status_table,
  caption = paste(
    "Terminal status by run type and prior profile.",
    "Posterior inference is suppressed for final_nonclean rows."
  )
)
```

Across all profiles, 43 rows were `primary_clean`, 49 were `rescue_clean`,
four were `final_nonclean`, and 53 invoked the single allowed rescue.

```{r}
#| label: table-status-by-cell
display_status_by_cell <- status_by_cell |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned` = format_count(
      primary_clean + rescue_clean,
      planned
    ),
    `Observed richness median (range)` = paste0(
      formatC(observed_richness_median, format = "f", digits = 1L),
      " (", observed_richness_range, ")"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Cell` = cell_id,
    `Known truth` = true_richness,
    `Occasions` = n_occasions,
    `Duration` = duration,
    `Planned` = planned,
    `Primary clean` = primary_clean,
    `Rescue clean` = rescue_clean,
    `Final non-clean` = final_nonclean,
    `Rescues` = rescues,

  )
knitr::kable(
  display_status_by_cell,
  caption = paste(
    "All frozen cells and profiles.",
    "Truth is a simulation label; observed richness is the data lower bound."
  )
)
```

## Prior-predictive evidence and PI decision

Before development and frozen recovery, each profile used 10,000 fixed-seed
prior draws. All 21 unchanged automatic numerical and design-informativeness
rules passed. The evidence ID is
`893ed2149d3608d8f62ce369c48337df46bbbc882e9cf86ba698307b1daf540d`.

```{r}
#| label: table-prior-decision
prior_decision <- prior_manifest |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `PI verdict` = "accept_provisionally",
    `Verdict date (UTC)` = dplyr::case_when(
      profile_id == "sensitivity-tail-v2" ~ "2026-07-30",
      TRUE ~ "2026-07-28"
    ),
    `Automatic rules` = vapply(
      profile_key,
      function(key) {
        rows <- prior_assessment$profile_key == key
        format_count(sum(prior_assessment$passed[rows]), sum(rows))
      },
      character(1)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Profile role` = profile_key,
    `Profile ID` = profile_id,
    `Draws` = n_draws,
    `Simulation seed` = simulation_seed,
    `Automatic rules`,
    `Automatic outcome` = automatic_outcome,
    `PI verdict`,
    `Verdict date (UTC)`
  )
knitr::kable(
  prior_decision,
  caption = paste(
    "Prior-predictive numerical evidence and explicit PI verdicts.",
    "Provisional acceptance was restricted to this synthetic pilot."
  )
)
```

The accepted tail sensitivity is `sensitivity-tail-v2`
(\(\mu_\alpha\) scale 2.5, \(\sigma_\alpha\) scale 1.75), following the one
permitted pre-recovery revision. An automatic pass was not treated as an
ecological judgement.

## HMC diagnostics and rescue use

A terminal clean fit required zero divergences, zero maximum-treedepth hits,
minimum E-BFMI at least 0.3, maximum \(\widehat R\) at most 1.01, and minimum
bulk and tail ESS at least 400 for all monitored continuous quantities,
including the Rao--Blackwellised richness summaries.

```{r}
#| label: table-diagnostic-summary
display_diagnostics <- diagnostic_summary |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Terminal status` = terminal_status,
    `Rows` = rows,
    `Max divergences` = maximum_divergences,
    `Max treedepth hits` = maximum_treedepth_hits,
    `Min E-BFMI` = minimum_ebfmi,
    `Max R-hat` = maximum_rhat,
    `Min bulk ESS` = minimum_bulk_ess,
    `Min tail ESS` = minimum_tail_ess
  )
knitr::kable(
  display_diagnostics,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Terminal-attempt diagnostics by run type, profile and status.",
    "The extrema describe each displayed status group."
  )
)
```

The four-year membership-sensitivity failure had minimum tail ESS
288.803 after rescue. It remains in all status and gate denominators.

## Four-year recovery by true-richness cell

All three four-year primary cells were terminal-clean in 10/10 rows and had
90% interval coverage in 10/10 rows. The table remains cell-level: pooled
summaries do not replace it.

```{r}
#| label: table-four-year-recovery
four_year_table <- primary_cell |>
  dplyr::filter(n_occasions == 208L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned` = format_count(clean_n, planned_n),
    `Observed median (range)` = paste0(
      formatC(observed_median, format = "f", digits = 1L),
      " (", observed_range, ")"
    ),
    `Posterior mean median (range)` = paste0(
      formatC(posterior_mean_median, format = "f", digits = 2L),
      " (", posterior_mean_range, ")"
    ),
    `90% coverage` = format_count(coverage_90, planned_n)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Cell` = cell_id,
    `Known truth` = true_richness,
    `Observed median (range)`,
    `Posterior mean median (range)`,
    `Clean/planned`,
    `Rescues` = rescues_n,
    `90% coverage`,
    `Median posterior abs. error` = median_absolute_error,
    `Median observed abs. error` = raw_median_absolute_error,
    `Median 90% width` = median_interval_width
  )
knitr::kable(
  four_year_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Four-year primary recovery in each known-truth cell.",
    "Posterior summaries use clean fits; gate errors retain fixed denominators."
  )
)
```

Across the 30 four-year primary rows, the posterior mean's median absolute
error was 1.096702 species, below the two-species gate but above the raw
observed-richness median absolute error of 1. The posterior was individually
closer to truth in 18/30 rows, but Criterion 27 compares medians and therefore
failed.

## Six-month partial-information behaviour

The six-month cells contain 30 planned primary rows and 29 clean posterior
summaries. The retained non-clean primary row is a noncoverage and receives
the frozen error penalties; it does not contribute a posterior mean or
interval width.

```{r}
#| label: table-six-month-recovery
six_month_table <- primary_cell |>
  dplyr::filter(n_occasions == 26L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned` = format_count(clean_n, planned_n),
    `Observed median (range)` = paste0(
      formatC(observed_median, format = "f", digits = 1L),
      " (", observed_range, ")"
    ),
    `Posterior mean median (range)` = paste0(
      formatC(posterior_mean_median, format = "f", digits = 2L),
      " (", posterior_mean_range, ")"
    ),
    `90% coverage` = format_count(coverage_90, planned_n)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Cell` = cell_id,
    `Known truth` = true_richness,
    `Observed median (range)`,
    `Posterior mean median (range)`,
    `Clean/planned`,
    `Final non-clean` = nonclean_n,
    `Rescues` = rescues_n,
    `90% coverage`,
    `Median frozen abs. error` = median_absolute_error,
    `Median observed abs. error` = raw_median_absolute_error,
    `Median clean 90% width` = median_interval_width
  )
knitr::kable(
  six_month_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Six-month primary behaviour in each known-truth cell.",
    "Wide posterior ranges express partial information rather than sharp identification."
  )
)
```

The 90% interval covered truth in 28/30 scheduled rows. This is a coarse
pilot screen, not evidence of nominal calibration. No hard six-month
point-accuracy or sharpness threshold was applied.

## Full posterior RPS versus the lower-bound-conditioned comparator

The comparator conditions on detected candidates being members but ignores
all zero-detection histories, effort and encounter likelihood. It therefore
shares the observed-richness lower bound. The unnormalised discrete ranked
probability score (RPS; lower is better) compares full richness
distributions, not just point estimates.

```{r}
#| label: table-four-year-rps
rps_table <- primary |>
  dplyr::filter(n_occasions == 208L) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    run_type, profile_id, cell_id, true_richness, n_occasions
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    planned = dplyr::n(),
    clean = sum(clean),
    posterior_better = sum(rps < baseline_rps),
    median_posterior_rps = stats::median(rps),
    median_comparator_rps = stats::median(baseline_rps),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned` = format_count(clean, planned),
    `Posterior better` = format_count(posterior_better, planned)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Cell` = cell_id,
    `Known truth` = true_richness,
    `Clean/planned`,
    `Posterior better`,
    `Median posterior RPS` = median_posterior_rps,
    `Median comparator RPS` = median_comparator_rps
  )
knitr::kable(
  rps_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Four-year full-distribution RPS by known-truth cell."
)
```

The pooled frozen gate used all 30 scheduled four-year primary rows: median
posterior RPS was 0.604592 versus 9.093747 for the comparator, and the
posterior RPS was smaller in 29/30 rows. This does not establish superiority
to an empirical estimator or to a separately fitted model.

## Prior sensitivity

Sensitivity shifts compare paired posterior means with the matching primary
run. Rows whose sensitivity or paired primary fit is terminal non-clean use
the frozen candidate-pool-sized sentinel of 30 and remain uninterpreted.

```{r}
#| label: table-sensitivity
display_sensitivity <- sensitivity_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned pairs` = format_count(clean_pairs, planned_pairs)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Duration` = duration,
    `Occasions` = n_occasions,
    `Clean/planned pairs`,
    `Non-clean pairs` = nonclean_pairs,
    `Median shift, frozen policy` = median_shift_frozen,
    `Maximum shift, frozen policy` = maximum_shift_frozen,
    `Median shift, clean pairs` = median_shift_clean,
    `Maximum shift, clean pairs` = maximum_shift_clean
  )
knitr::kable(
  display_sensitivity,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Paired prior sensitivity by duration and profile.",
    "Frozen-policy columns include the non-clean sentinel where applicable."
  )
)
```

Clean four-year shifts were small: membership-profile median 0.173871
(8/9 clean pairs), tail-profile median 0.200727 (9/9), and tail maximum
1.009819. Nevertheless, one four-year membership sensitivity was
`final_nonclean`; the frozen sentinel of 30 makes Criteria 33 and 34 fail.
The value 30 is a penalty, not a fitted 30-species displacement.

## Posterior predictive checks

For every terminal-clean row, posterior predictive summaries retain total,
candidate-level and camera-level detection counts. The table below compares
the observed total with the posterior replicated distribution. Non-clean rows
are counted but have no posterior predictive product.

```{r}
#| label: table-ppc
display_ppc <- ppc_by_cell |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Clean/planned` = format_count(clean, planned),
    `Observed within replicated 90%` = format_count(ppc_90, clean)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    `Run type` = run_type,
    `Prior profile` = profile_id,
    `Known truth` = true_richness,
    `Duration` = duration,
    `Clean/planned`,
    `Final non-clean` = final_nonclean,
    `Observed richness median` = observed_richness_median,
    `Posterior mean richness median` = posterior_mean_richness_median,
    `Observed detections median` = observed_detections_median,
    `Replicated detections median` = replicated_detections_median,
    `Observed within replicated 90%`
  )
knitr::kable(
  display_ppc,
  digits = 2,
  caption = paste(
    "Posterior predictive total-detection checks by profile and cell.",
    "Truth, observation, posterior inference and terminal status are separated."
  )
)
```

These checks assess consistency with the fitted correctly specified
observation model. They cannot diagnose untested misspecification, incomplete
candidate pools, false positives, temporal turnover or spatial dependence.

## Every acceptance gate, including failures

The table records all 41 Goal criteria. Criteria 19--35 are the immutable
frozen gate records; the remaining rows are explicit implementation,
prior-predictive and Task 12 closure checks. A failure is retained as evidence
and is not converted into a pass by a descriptive clean-only analysis.

```{r}
#| label: table-all-criteria
knitr::kable(
  criteria_table,
  caption = paste(
    "Complete Goal 002 acceptance ledger.",
    "Fraction is numerator/denominator under the criterion's stated contract."
  )
)
```

The frozen scientific subset passed 14/17 gates and failed 3/17. Criterion
27 failed the prespecified strict comparison of median absolute errors.
Criteria 33 and 34 failed because the non-clean four-year membership
sensitivity must receive the frozen sentinel and remain uninterpreted.

## Limitations and Goal 003 recommendation

The pilot has only 10 primary replicates per cell and three paired
sensitivities per cell. Membership and the lower encounter-rate tail remain
weakly identified when candidates are never detected. Rescue use was common
(53/96 rows), and four rows remained non-clean. The results cover only the
correctly specified Goal 001 process with a finite known candidate pool,
Gaussian log-rate effects, nine cameras and two durations.

Deferred work includes misspecified encounter distributions,
membership--detectability dependence, temporal and spatial dependence,
candidate-pool uncertainty, false positives, other occasion lengths,
sampling-intensity curves, classical or hierarchical comparators, empirical
Judbury data and all Huon Ridge data. None should be added to Goal 002 to
rescue the failed gate.

**Recommendation:** stop this model version at the informative failure.
Goal 003 planning should begin with a PI-level model-repair decision. A
revised, newly frozen study may test misspecification, sampling intensity and
comparators. If the priority is the non-clean membership/low-rate geometry,
consider the already specified exact unseen-richness enumeration with checked
Gauss--Hermite integration under a new design, new oracles and explicit PI
approval. Do not proceed directly to empirical analysis.
